newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-BALLESTEROS VOWS TO WIN AGAIN NEXT CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BALLESTEROS VOWS TO WIN AGAIN NEXT CENTURY.

text.p: Struggling Spaniard Severiano Ballesteros had his best round of the year at the Spanish Open on Thursday to give himself the chance of making his first cut in seven starts.
Europe's Ryder Cup captain shot a two-under par 70 to finish four strokes behind joint leaders Padraig Harrington of Ireland and Germany's Alexander Cejka.
Ballesteros, with 72 titles worldwide -- five of them majors -- was so pleased with his round that he insisted he will be a winner again -- in the next millenium.
"It has hurt and it has been tough playing badly recently, but I still believe I can be a winner," said Ballesteros. "I won in the 70s, 80s and 90s and can in 2,000s.

"I have a passion for this game, especially when I see all the people supporting me and there are always plenty of reasons to continue. Ask Arnold Palmer why. He has had a cancer operation at 67 and he was still there at the Masters. Why should I quit at 40? I have the feeling that some people think I should, but not me.

Ballesteros credits Tiger Woods' coach Butch Harmon with some of his change in fortune. "I worked with Butch during the Masters and at home in Santander and the best thing about it is that we're working on the same things. Before, I was always changing too many things, not good for me. Now there is less stress mentally."

Ballesteros ran up six birdies in his round and had moved to within a stroke of the early lead by the 11th, despite going into water at the sixth. But bogeys on the 13th and 14th denied him the score he thought he deserved.

"The way I played was worth more than a 70. I was unlucky at the sixth and then lost concentration at the end. One of the most difficult things in golf is to concentrate for 4-1/2 hours. All my birdies were through good shots today."
